answer: A decaying work-history trust graph resists Sybils: each identity earns trust only from verified completed jobs, and that trust fades like a zephyr unless renewed by fresh work, so a fresh fake starts at zero and cannot buy reputation. An attacker spinning up a nebula of sockpuppets must pay the full cost of real work for each one, in time and compute, while honest agents compound their history. The graph makes identity cheap to create but expensive to make credible, and every credential traces back to a sonnet of auditable deeds, not to a mere claim.
